what: WebGL layer behind the screen — the noise height map is sliced into 24 thin slabs and stacked (each slab keeps only areas higher than its height) to make gray contour steps, then a shadow sampled offset away from the light and a light-side highlight are added. For the first 3s the camera moves to the path’s 0→2s position, then follows scroll progress between the start and end markers at .075 per frame, descending to the 2→8.9s position — the FOV widens 70→124° as it drops into the steps, a rainbow color tied to layer height (0→2.48) fills in, and edge chromatic aberration widens −.15→−.54. At 10.27s the steps vanish, and when the footer marker enters, a different set of steps on the path at 11→13s turns on. Grain .1, bottom darkening (.5 → 0 until progress 15%). Cursor: a 128-cell fluid velocity map (brush radius .035 of screen, motion ×4.23, .9324 applied twice per frame → half-life about 83ms) lights the layers where it passed (hero .057, footer .07 ×5) and jitters layer edges by .004. The camera pivots toward the cursor around a point 1.196 in front of the screen (follows at .032 and .025 per frame, the angle is the path look, and the difference of the two ×.1 is the tilt). On phones, finger drag changes brightness only, and it is off under reduced motion.

options.start · end: Selectors for the start and end markers that measure scroll progress — 0 when the top edge of the start marker reaches the top of the screen, 1 when the bottom edge of the end marker reaches it
options.footer: Marker selector that turns on the footer steps — 0 when the top edge touches the bottom of the screen, 1 when it touches the top
options.lerp: Share that follows scroll (per Frame), default .075
options.intro: Initial duration (sec) for the camera to reach the first spot, default 3
options.wait: If true, the entrance starts when fx:go is received
options.--fx-contour-bg · --fx-contour-base · --: Background · stair surface · footer stair surface · shadow · highlight colors, default --kf-bg · ink at 78% · 69% · 30% · --kf-ink
options.fx:seq: Event fired every frame by the element — detail.pos is the position on the path (seconds). Draws the path-bound text (”You jump…”) at this position

use: — Load three-global.js before three.cjs(0.162)
note: The original draws the height map with two layers of simplex noise and the colors as five stages built with Theatre. Here, a height map mixing three layers of value noise with a center well shape, plus a rainbow band tied to layer height, gives the same look. Camera, height, shadow, color and chromatic aberration keyframe values, plus cursor fluid and camera orbit values, are exactly the original Home scene (the shader is ours)
